messages:
From: Lisa Park <lisa.park@stellarishealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@stellarishealth.com
Date: 2028-07-11T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Procurement RFP - Export & Safeguards Appendix

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. As part of our procurement packet for the RFP, our legal and privacy teams asked for a short appendix that specifically addresses international data exports, DPF/appropriate safeguards, and the operational evidence we can include in the security pack.

Attached is the Stellaris export questionnaire and a template table for controls mapping. Our key asks are: a) a concise narrative on how Redwood implements technical & contractual safeguards for EU->US processing, b) an evidence bundle we can share with our Data Protection Officer (sample logs, pseudonymization approach, retention policy extract), and c) whether Redwood can commit to an addendum to the DPA for our procurement terms (we will share draft redlines next week).

Timeline: procurement would like completed appendix + evidence by Friday 2028-07-15 to proceed to the commercial committee. Can you advise feasibility and who from Redwood we should expect responses from?

Thanks,
Lisa Park
Procurement Manager
Stellaris Health
[Attachment: stellaris-export-questionnaire.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet) - 45 KB]

From: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@stellarishealth.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-07-12T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement RFP - Export & Safeguards Appendix

Hi Lisa — thanks, and appreciate the clear asks.

Short answer on feasibility: yes, we can deliver a concise export/safeguards appendix and an evidence bundle by 2028-07-15. Im putting Soojin (security & privacy) and Marissa (solutions/ops) on the thread to coordinate the evidence pack and the DPA addendum response.

What we will provide by Friday:
- A 2-page narrative that explains Redwoods cross-border safeguards (legal basis, SCCs/DPF routing, encryption in transit/at rest, subprocessor controls).
- A populated controls mapping table (your template).
- Sample pseudonymized flow logs (CSV) and a sanitized retention policy extract.
- A draft DPA addendum showing where we can accept procurement redlines and where we need standard language.

Attachments I will include in the Friday package: redwood-export-safeguards-appendix.pdf (narrative + table), sample-pseudologs.csv (sanitized examples), rdw-dpf-mapping.xlsx (technical mapping).

Sooj, Marissa: can you confirm you can turn the evidence/attachments around by end of day Thursday so Ben can assemble Friday?

Lisa: quick Q on jurisdiction — are you seeking a technical routing control (guarantee of EU-only processing) or are you evaluating contractual/transfer mechanisms (DPF/SCCs with supplemental technical safeguards)? We can accommodate either with different tradeoffs.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none in this message]

From: soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
To: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Lisa Park <lisa.park@stellarishealth.com>
Date: 2028-07-13T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement RFP - Export & Safeguards Appendix

Ben / Marissa — confirming we can deliver the artifacts. Notes on content and redlines:

1) Routing & DPF: Redwood does not offer an architectural "EU-only processing" guarantee for all models in our hosted plan due to multi-region fallbacks and caching; we do provide region pinning for Dedicated/Private and can document routing policies and fallbacks. For the RFP appendix we'll include:
   - Our DPF alignment statement (how we rely on SCCs + supplementary technical measures where DPF is triggered).
   - Examples of Smart Routing policy configuration customers use to enforce EU-only processing (Dedicated/Private) and how we enforce region affinity in the control plane.

2) Technical safeguards: include AES-256 at rest, TLS1.3 in transit, per-customer KV cache separation, and token-level auditability. We'll add a short sample audit log showing request/region/processing-node (sanitized).

3) Pseudonymization & logs: sample-pseudologs.csv will be sanitized to remove PII (IDs hashed with salted HMAC). We'll include a short readme that explains sanitization steps.

4) DPA addendum: we are generally open to limited redline acceptance for procurement clauses (retention, subprocessor list updates, and SOC2 upload references). We cannot accept unconstrained liability expansion; will propose a compromise clause and add a narrow SLA deviation for data residency for an added fee or Dedicated deployment.

Marissa: Ive attached a checklist for the pack and a small sample of the sanitized log. Ben, please merge with the narrative.

-Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sample-pseudologs.csv (text/csv) - 32 KB]
